page: OVHcloud l4-90 is a specialized GPU cloud instance within the Cloud GPU family, engineered to accelerate AI inference, graphics processing, and compute workloads. Powered by a dedicated 22-core AMD EPYC 9454 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the system operates with one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. It features 90 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 4.09 GB per core, along with 400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface running under a KVM hypervisor. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of GDDR6 VRAM based on the Ada Lovelace architecture.

Benchmark evaluations show exceptional artificial intelligence inference performance on small and medium language models. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved top-tier throughput in prompt processing and text generation for 135M and 7B parameter models, reaching 2,286.1 prompt tokens per second and 54.36 generation tokens per second on 7B models. In CPU evaluations, the AMD EPYC silicon scored in the top ten percent for single-core stress-ng workloads (3,155.89) and demonstrated strong multi-core processing with a score of 68,513.44. Vector instructions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 provide further computational acceleration for numeric processing.

From an efficiency perspective, the single-GPU architecture balances high-density Ada Lovelace tensor processing with dedicated host resources, avoiding the overhead of massive multi-GPU configurations. The 24 GB VRAM limit and 400 GB local NVMe storage restrict large-scale 70B parameter model serving and sprawling data sets, but provide sufficient headroom for lightweight model inference, computer vision, video transcoding, and medium-scale enterprise machine learning pipelines.

Equipped with 90 GB of system memory, 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and an 8 Gbps baseline network connection, the instance delivers balanced host and accelerator specifications. Benchmarks place the server in the top tier for lightweight and medium-sized language model inference, registering 2,286.1 prompt tokens per second on 7B models alongside strong single-core and multi-core CPU compute scores. Vector extensions such as AVX-512 BF16 and VNNI augment on-chip operations. The configuration represents an efficient resource envelope for organizations running real-time AI inference, video processing, computer vision, and machine learning model serving.
